subject: Reading
skill_name: Hear the first sound in a spoken word
teach_text: Listen for the sound that starts the word. Say the word slowly and tap the first sound.
worked_example: Word: sun. First sound: /s/.
q1_prompt: What is the first sound in "map"?
q1_hint: Say map slowly. What do your lips do first?
q2_prompt: What is the first sound in "top"?
q2_hint: The first sound is the one you hear before the middle vowel.
q3_prompt: What is the first sound in "ship"?
q3_hint: Ship starts with two letters that make one sound.
q4_prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as "fan"?
q4_choices: sun|van|mop
q4_hint: Listen for /f/. Which other word has that starting sound?

subject: Reading
skill_name: Blend two sounds into a word
teach_text: Put the sounds together without a pause. /c/ + /at/ becomes cat.
worked_example: Sounds: /s/ /u/ /n/ → sun
q1_prompt: Blend /m/ /e/.
q1_choices: me|am|em
q1_hint: Say the first sound then slide into the second.
q2_prompt: Blend /g/ /o/.
q2_hint: Keep the /g/ short then say /o/.
q3_prompt: Blend /sh/ /oe/.
q3_choices: show|osh|shoe
q3_hint: The first sound is /sh/ like in ship.
q4_prompt: Blend /s/ /t/ /ar/.
q4_choices: rats|star|tars
q4_hint: Three sounds. Start with /s/ then /t/.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Match letter to its common sound
teach_text: Each letter has a name and a sound. We use the sound when we read.
worked_example: Letter m says /m/ like moon.
q1_prompt: What sound does the letter s usually make?
q1_hint: Think of sun or snake.
q2_prompt: What sound does the letter b usually make?
q2_hint: Your lips come together then pop open.
q3_prompt: Which letter makes the /k/ sound in cat?
q3_choices: c|s|m
q3_hint: Cat starts with the letter that can say /k/.
q4_prompt: Which letter does NOT usually say /n/?
q4_choices: n|m|kn as in know wait — pick m
column32: Say each letter sound. Which one is not /n/?

subject: Reading
skill_name: Read CVC short-a words
teach_text: Short a sounds like /a/ in apple. Blend the three sounds.
worked_example: c-a-t → cat
q1_prompt: What word is m-a-t?
q1_choices: mat|met|mad
q1_hint: The middle letter is a. It says /a/.
q2_prompt: What word is s-a-t?
q2_hint: Keep the short a in the middle.
q3_prompt: Which word has the same middle sound as cap?
q3_choices: cup|cop|map
q3_hint: Short a is the sound in apple.
q4_prompt: Read this word: plan. Wait — which is a short-a CVC word?
q4_choices: plan|pan|pain
q4_hint: CVC means consonant-vowel-consonant. Three letters.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Read words with silent e (a_e)
teach_text: When a word has a vowel plus a consonant plus silent e the first vowel often says its name.
worked_example: cape = /k/ /ā/ /p/. The e is quiet.
q1_prompt: What does cap become if you add e?
q1_choices: cape|cap|cope
q1_hint: Silent e can make a say its name.
q2_prompt: Which word has a long a?
q2_hint: Look for the silent e at the end.
q3_prompt: Read: tape. What is the vowel sound?
q3_choices: short a|long a|short e
q3_hint: The e at the end is silent and the a says its name.
q4_prompt: Which pair shows the silent-e change?
q4_choices: mad / made|sit / sat|hop / hip
q4_hint: Only one pair adds silent e and changes the vowel.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Read common grade-1 sight words
teach_text: Sight words are words we see so often we read them in one look.
worked_example: the said you they
q1_prompt: Which word is "said"?
q1_choices: sad|said|sand
q1_hint: It looks a little like sad but has i in the middle.
q2_prompt: Which sentence uses a sight word correctly?
q2_choices: They is running.|They are running.|Them are running.
q2_hint: They needs the verb are.
q3_prompt: Find the sight word: We went to the park.
q3_choices: park|went|the
q3_hint: The is a small high-frequency word.
q4_prompt: Which is NOT a sight word you memorize as a picture?
q4_choices: the|said|cat
q4_hint: Cat you can sound out. Sight words often break the usual rules.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Read a short sentence smoothly
teach_text: Fluency means reading like talking — not one choppy word at a time.
worked_example: The cat sat. → said as one thought not The. Cat. Sat.
q1_prompt: Which reading is smoother?
q1_choices: The. dog. ran.|The dog ran.|THE DOG RAN
q1_hint: Smooth reading groups words together.
q2_prompt: What should you do at a period?
q2_choices: keep going|stop and take a breath|speed up
q2_hint: A period is a full stop.
q3_prompt: Which mark tells you a sentence is a question?
q3_hint: A question mark means your voice should go up.
q4_prompt: To read fluently you should
q4_choices: guess every word|reread a sentence that sounded choppy|skip hard words
q4_answer: reread a sentence that sounded choppy
q4_hint: Rereading is how fluency grows.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Use context to guess a new word
teach_text: The other words in the sentence give clues.
worked_example: The pup was tiny. Tiny means very small.
q1_prompt: The soup was scalding so we waited. Scalding means
q1_choices: cold|very hot|sweet
q1_hint: You wait when something might burn.
q2_prompt: Maya was exhausted after the long hike. Exhausted means
q2_hint: A long hike makes your body tired.
q3_prompt: Which clue word helps most in: The cavern was dark and damp.
q3_choices: was|dark|and
q3_hint: Dark and damp describe the cavern.
q4_prompt: The kitten was timid and hid. Timid means
q4_choices: brave|shy|loud
q4_hint: Hiding is a clue that timid is not brave.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Retell the beginning middle and end
teach_text: Stories have a start, a middle problem or event, and an ending.
worked_example: Goldilocks goes in → tries the bowls → runs home
q1_prompt: A story beginning usually
q1_choices: solves the problem|introduces who and where|lists vocabulary
q1_hint: The start tells us who the story is about.
q2_prompt: The middle of a story often has
q2_choices: the title|a problem or important event|the author's name
q2_hint: Something happens in the middle.
q3_prompt: After you read you should be able to
q3_choices: retell what happened in order|name every adjective|skip the ending
q3_hint: Order means beginning then middle then end.
q4_prompt: Which is an ending?
q4_choices: Once there was a fox.|The fox found a lock.|The fox opened the gate and walked free.
q4_answer: The fox opened the gate and walked free.
q4_hint: An ending wraps up the problem.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Name the main idea of a short paragraph
teach_text: The main idea is what the whole paragraph is mostly about. Details support it.
worked_example: Paragraph about bees making honey → main idea: bees make honey.
q1_prompt: Bees fly from flower to flower. They collect nectar. Then they make honey. Main idea?
q1_choices: Bees have wings.|Bees make honey.|Flowers are yellow.
q1_hint: Ask: what is the whole paragraph about?
q2_prompt: A detail is
q2_choices: the big idea|a small fact that supports the idea|the title only
q2_answer: a small fact that supports the idea
q2_hint: Details prove or explain the main idea.
q3_prompt: Which sentence is a detail not a main idea?
q3_choices: Owls are nighttime hunters.|An owl can turn its head far around.|Owls hunt at night and have special bodies for it.
q3_answer: An owl can turn its head far around.
q3_hint: One body fact is a detail.
q4_prompt: Main idea should cover
q4_choices: one tiny fact|most of the sentences|only the first word
q4_hint: If most sentences fit it you have the main idea.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Identify the narrator
teach_text: Ask: who is telling this story? I/we is first person. He/she is third.
worked_example: I ran to the dock. → first person
q1_prompt: I packed my bag and waited. Who is telling the story?
q1_choices: a narrator outside the story|the character using I|the reader
q1_hint: The word I is the clue.
q2_prompt: Which is third person?
q2_choices: I was late.|She was late.|We were late.
q2_hint: She means someone else is being described.
q3_prompt: Why does narrator matter?
q3_choices: It changes whose thoughts we hear.|It changes the font.|It changes the page number.
q3_answer: It changes whose thoughts we hear.
q3_hint: First person lets us inside one character's head.
q4_prompt: A story that says "Marcus thought the test was easy" is
q4_choices: first person|second person|third person
q4_hint: We see Marcus from the outside.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Find the main idea of an informational paragraph
teach_text: Informational text teaches. The main idea is the lesson of the paragraph.
worked_example: Florida is a peninsula. That fact may support a paragraph about Florida's geography.
q1_prompt: Alligators live in freshwater. They are reptiles. They bask in the sun. Main idea?
q1_choices: Alligators are freshwater reptiles.|The sun is hot.|Reptiles have scales.
q1_hint: Combine the facts into one statement.
q2_prompt: Signal words like for example often introduce
q2_hint: Examples support the main idea.
q3_prompt: Which title best matches a paragraph about how hurricanes form?
q3_choices: My Beach Trip|How Hurricanes Form|Types of Lizards
q3_hint: A good title names the main idea.
q4_prompt: A sentence that does not belong should be
q4_choices: kept anyway|removed as extra|used as the title
q4_hint: Off-topic sentences hide the main idea.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Recognize sequence in a text
teach_text: Sequence texts use first next then finally or numbered steps.
worked_example: First mix. Next bake. Finally cool.
q1_prompt: Which words show sequence?
q1_choices: however because|first next finally|similarly unlike
q1_hint: Sequence words put events in time order.
q2_prompt: What comes after "first" in a how-to?
q2_hint: Steps move forward.
q3_prompt: A recipe is usually organized by
q3_choices: compare and contrast|sequence|problem and solution
q3_hint: You follow steps in order.
q4_prompt: Which is out of order for planting a seed?
q4_choices: dig a hole → drop seed → cover → water|water → drop seed on concrete → wait|label the pot last
q4_answer: dig a hole → drop seed → cover → water
q4_hint: Think about what must happen before the seed can grow.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Decide if a text informs persuades or entertains
teach_text: Authors write to teach to convince or to tell a story that entertains.
worked_example: A science article informs. An ad persuades. A funny story entertains.
q1_prompt: A chapter explaining how volcanoes erupt is meant to
q1_choices: entertain|inform|persuade
q1_hint: It teaches facts.
q2_prompt: A commercial that says you should buy Brain Kit is meant to
q2_hint: Persuade means the author wants you to do or believe something.
q3_prompt: A tall-tale about a giant fox is mainly meant to
q3_choices: entertain|give directions|list standards
q3_hint: Stories that delight are written to entertain.
q4_prompt: An article that gives both facts and a call to recycle is
q4_choices: only entertainment|inform and persuade|a poem
q4_hint: Some texts have more than one purpose. Pick the best pair.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Identify a simile
teach_text: A simile compares two things using like or as.
worked_example: The cloud was like cotton.
q1_prompt: Which sentence is a simile?
q1_choices: The wind howled.|The wind was as sharp as glass.|It is windy.
q1_answer: The wind was as sharp as glass.
q1_hint: Look for like or as.
q2_prompt: Kit is as quick as a spark compares Kit to
q2_hint: The second thing in the comparison is the spark.
q3_prompt: Which uses like?
q3_choices: She is a rock.|She ran like the wind.|She ran.
q3_hint: Like is the clue word.
q4_prompt: A simile is different from a metaphor because a simile
q4_choices: never compares|uses like or as|is always about weather
q4_hint: Metaphors say something is something else.

subject: Reading
skill_name: State a theme in a short story
teach_text: Theme is the big idea about life the story suggests. It is not just the plot.
worked_example: Plot: a girl shares her lunch. Theme: kindness matters.
q1_prompt: A boy practices piano every day and finally plays the song. A theme could be
q1_choices: pianos are black|practice helps you grow|Monday is a day
q1_hint: Theme is a lesson you could use in real life.
q2_prompt: Theme is not the same as
q2_choices: a life lesson|a one-sentence plot summary|an idea about friendship or courage
q2_hint: Plot is what happens. Theme is what it means.
q3_prompt: Which is written as a theme?
q3_choices: Marcus lost the race.|Hard work beats talent when talent does not work.|There was a race.
q3_answer: Hard work beats talent when talent does not work.
q3_hint: Theme is a general statement.
q4_prompt: A good theme should
q4_choices: name every character|apply beyond this one story|list page numbers
q4_hint: If it only works for this plot it is not yet a theme.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Use prefixes un- and re-
teach_text: un- often means not or opposite. re- often means again.
worked_example: unhappy = not happy. rebuild = build again.
q1_prompt: What does unhappy mean?
q1_choices: very happy|not happy|happy again
q1_hint: un- can flip the meaning.
q2_prompt: Rewrite means
q2_hint: re- points to again.
q3_prompt: Which word means the opposite of lock?
q3_choices: relock|unlock|locking
q3_hint: Opposite is the un- job.
q4_prompt: If you reread a page you
q4_choices: read it again|refuse to read|read a new book
q4_hint: re- + read.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Adjust rate for a hard informational paragraph
teach_text: Slow down on new words and dense facts. Speed back up when the text is familiar.
worked_example: A science paragraph deserves a slower first read.
q1_prompt: When a paragraph is packed with new facts you should
q1_choices: skip it|slow down on the first read|race
q1_answer: slow down on the first read
q1_hint: New information needs more time.
q2_prompt: Fluency includes
q2_choices: only speed|accuracy phrasing and rate|memorizing fonts
q2_hint: Speed without accuracy is not fluency.
q3_prompt: A good reason to reread is
q3_choices: the paragraph felt confusing|you finished early|the page is even
q3_hint: Confusion is a signal to try again slower.
q4_prompt: Which is a fluency goal?
q4_choices: sounding like speech with understanding|finishing first|skipping punctuation
q4_hint: Understanding is the point.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Read kindergarten high-frequency words
teach_text: Some words we know by looking: I a the see.
worked_example: I see the cat.
q1_prompt: Which word is "the"?
q1_choices: teh|the|hte
q1_hint: The is t-h-e.
q2_prompt: Find I: I can hop.
q2_hint: I is one letter and a word.
q3_prompt: Which sentence uses see?
q3_choices: I see a fox.|I sea a fox.|I se a fox.
q3_hint: See is s-e-e.
q4_prompt: A high-frequency word is one you
q4_choices: almost never meet|meet in many books|only see in math
q4_hint: High-frequency means it shows up a lot.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Use a glossary or nearby sentence to define a word
teach_text: If a word is new look at the sentence or a glossary in the back of the book.
worked_example: Habitat: the place an animal lives.
q1_prompt: A glossary is usually
q1_choices: on the cover|an alphabetical list of word meanings|a map
q1_answer: an alphabetical list of word meanings
q1_hint: Glossaries work like a mini dictionary for that book.
q2_prompt: In "The arid desert gets almost no rain" arid means
q2_hint: Almost no rain is the clue.
q3_prompt: You should try context first because
q3_choices: it is faster than guessing randomly|glossaries are illegal|pictures never help
q3_answer: it is faster than guessing randomly
q3_hint: The sentence is sitting right there.
q4_prompt: Which source fits a domain word in a science book?
q4_choices: a glossary entry|a joke book|the page number alone
q4_hint: Science books often define their own terms.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Distinguish main idea from supporting details in a two-paragraph text
teach_text: First find what each paragraph is about then name what the whole text is about.
worked_example: Para 1: manatees eat plants. Para 2: boats can hurt them. Whole: manatees need protection in Florida waters.
q1_prompt: Two paragraphs describe manatee food and boat injuries. Whole-text main idea?
q1_choices: Manatees eat.|Manatees face needs and dangers in the water.|Boats are fast.
q1_answer: Manatees face needs and dangers in the water.
q1_hint: Combine both paragraphs.
q2_prompt: A supporting detail should
q2_choices: open a new topic|prove or explain the main idea|replace the title
q2_answer: prove or explain the main idea
q2_hint: Details work for the main idea.
q3_prompt: If paragraph two does not fit paragraph one's idea the text may have
q3_choices: two related ideas under a bigger idea|no words|only pictures
q3_answer: two related ideas under a bigger idea
q3_hint: Zoom out one level.
q4_prompt: Which sentence is too narrow to be the whole-text main idea?
q4_choices: Florida manatees are plant-eating mammals that need safe water.|They eat seagrass.|A boat has a propeller.
q4_hint: One food fact cannot cover a whole article.

subject: Reading
skill_name: Identify a claim in a short news blurb
teach_text: A claim is what the writer wants you to accept as true.
worked_example: Claim: School start times should be later.
q1_prompt: What is a claim?
q1_choices: a question mark|a statement the writer wants you to accept|a caption font
q1_answer: a statement the writer wants you to accept
q1_hint: Claims can be argued.
q2_prompt: Which is a claim?
q2_choices: Water boils at 100 C at sea level is a fact often given.|Later start times help teens.|What time is it?
q2_hint: You could reasonably disagree with a claim.
q3_prompt: Evidence is
q3_choices: the writer's hat size|facts or examples that support the claim|the URL color
q3_answer: facts or examples that support the claim
q3_hint: Claims need backing.
q4_prompt: A news blurb without evidence should make you
q4_choices: stop thinking|ask what is missing|accept it
q4_hint: Missing evidence is a flag.
